For most licenses, including the GPL (GNU Public License), it is standard practice to include and PRESERVE the copyright info (name, website, email) for all contributors in the source. Under such licenses, the copyright is retained by the owner(s) but the license grants permission to copy, redistribute, and use the code for any purpose, including nefarious ones.

The fault rests entirely on the author for failing to understand the permission he has granted. There is absolutely no legal basis to sue (for using the code). Muller is free to distribute his work under any license he chooses, including one restricting the possible uses. However, the history of restrictive partially-open source licenses has demonstrated problems. There are damn good reasons why we choose the open source licenses we have. See the Debian Free Software Guidelines - INcompatible Licenses.

Update/clarification: With the common open source licenses, there is no basis to sue for using the code or publishing the code. There may or may not be other violations of the license involved that merit litigation.

Each time you try to make a downvote the system will check if you've been downvoting more than you upvote ( in terms of %). I assume this is to prevent people reaching 100CCP and then just spending their day downvoting non stop. It shouldn't impact a regular user, but if you're a heavy handed downvoter and your votes no longer seem to count this may be why.

The code which essentially cancels the downvote:

// this user is downvoting more than upvoting, don't register the downvote
if (User.IsUserCommentVotingMeanie(userWhichDownvoted))
 {
 return;
 }

To check if you're mean there's another function which checks the following (IsUserCommentVotingMeanie or IsUserSubmissionVotingMeanie):

// downvote ratio
var downvotePercentage = (double)commentDownvotes / totalCommentVotes * 100;

// upvote ratio
var upvotePercentage = (double)commentUpvotes / totalCommentVotes * 100;

return downvotePercentage > upvotePercentage;

Edit: Here's the IsUserCommentVotingMeanie lines on GitHub, link courtesy of /u/sodaxy
